items.note: Association organized at Larrow Green 1889, creamery 1891 (Story 2); Gideon Vose organizer and first president (Story 4).
Article seven: paid by pounds of butterfat not weight; the test at his own station counted (Story 2).
'This rule is what turned a measuring fault into lost money' (Story 2).
Only Wilbur Teague named as bookkeeper; Effie Loomis and Hobart Sill absent from Section A.
Son correct, but manager 'from 1911' (planted error); 1913 required.
Station-gain line, five and a quarter per cent, carried to general account, every year (Story 4). 1898 origin not stated but not bolded.
Skimming station seven miles up, opened 4 May 1896; glass borrowed from Larrow Green (Stories 1-2).
Only 'weighed, sampled, tested and separated'; no composite sample, no percent read on the neck after a fixed pipette charge anywhere in Section A.
Ammon & Sons, Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897.
Full invoice lines, 6 dozen pipettes marked 17.6 c.c., total $77.93.
'0.19 point, the same in every month, in the June flush and in February alike' (Story 2).
Nothing on the pipette being uncheckable without a burette / no burette in the county.
Ansel Keddie 1861-1934, 29 seasons 1896-1924, dismissed 30 April 1925.
Kept the station test book in his own hand from 1896.
3.61 given but the summary leaf's 1896 figure of 3.80 never appears in Section A; both figures required.
8 May-10 July, nine weeks, question mark all present, but result given only as 'markedly higher'; the bolded 3.80 is missing.
Orra nee Brant; Emmet Brant, largest farmer, Orra's brother.
1919 circular present, but Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement (tested as taught, cannot say why) absent; both required.
Died February 1934 uncleared; test book impounded March 1925, to the Historical Rooms 1959.
Hessel Bottom six farms; Emmet had the biggest place.
Weigh book from 1 January 1897; the two scales agreed.
First complaint on record 1902; gives 3.61 vs 3.78 and never states the Hollow-vs-Green gap as 0.19 (the 'deficiency 0.19' sentence right after it is ambiguous but not a stated conflation).
Committee came in Grigg's sleigh in January and reported in March, but the Jan-Feb-Mar 1908 sampling and Grigg as chairman are not stated.
200,000 lb at 3.42 present, but proportionality / richer herds losing more not stated in Section A (only in C2 and F).
To Roy 1929, lent to Ivy 1958, Hazel after 1962.
Alder Corners factory, Vessey County, Jerome Cudd present; Redlow Ridge never named (only 'over the ridge').
Four farms in the summer flush present, but the bolded 1915 start is missing.
'Jerome Cudd's Alder Corners test book is the independent record', factory in Vessey County: independence with two elements (county and artifact).
Same milk tested 0.19 lower at the station, every season.
Same milk from the same farms tested differently at the two buildings; used against the hay theory (Stories 3, 6).
Daughter, and figures copied for Ivy in 1958, but the bolded 'sixteen seasons' appears nowhere; 1941-1962 tenure only partly given.
Strawn's circuit given as from 1908 (NT-23 planted error); 1907 required.
Lactometer at every visit, never once found added water.
12 June 1923, calibrated burette, condemned the whole lot.
Says only that he 'recorded the condemnation but drew no inference'; that he wrote no figure for the deficiency is not stated.
Order dates correct, but the 1924 average given as 3.85 (planted error) instead of 3.80.
Crate in the loft over the intake room; notebooks to the state office in 1936, Farland library 1947, Ivy found the 1923 volume.
Petition January 1925.
Dates and the two weigh-room sittings correct, but chairman only 'an Ashlin attorney'; Alonzo Frick not named.
Water, theft, hay all argued before the 1925 board; board found no cause established.
Four books including Strawn's condemnation-year notebook; nobody set it beside the station records.
Dismissed 30 April 1925 before the finding; 4 May $3,800 'without admission', charged to the station account.
One fifth of $19,000 stated, but never says the award went to the same account the 'gain' had been accumulating in since 1898 (run quotes the gain as carried to the general account).
Ivy b. 1931, granddaughter, Farland, Vaught.
'Ivy brought the scattered records together': weigh book, notebook, Alder Corners figures, test book.
February 1958, station loft, nine surviving.
9 March 1958, 16.72 vs 17.6, 0.88 c.c., 5 per cent short.
5 per cent short; 3.61 recorded where true 3.80, 0.19 deficiency (Stories 1, 2, 4).
40,000,000 lb, 76,000 lb, $19,000 at 25c, and the 'gain' was 76,000 lb (Story 4).
Bulletin 471 October 1958; cleared 24 years after death, 33 after dismissal; crate 35 years in loft since 1923.
Granddaughter.
Duncan son of Ansel; Ivy Duncan's daughter.
Second cousins, derived via Emmet/Orra siblings and Roy/Duncan first cousins.
Declares full/half undeterminable, but then says half siblings would make them 'half second cousins', i.e. that it changes the answer; key requires that it does not.
Gideon Vose.
Gideon wrote article seven, the station-test rule that turned the fault into money loss; son defending father's institution.
Verdict sentence 'The best evidence says there was none'; the family denial is treated as outweighing hearsay. That is an assertion.
Asserting either way = 0; also treats a family denial as evidence rather than noting no record exists.
$90.00, explicitly using 25c period average instead of a 1910 price, with working: the key's accepted alternative.
76,000; 5.26% of credited, 5.00% of received, denominators named.
72 pipettes, 0.88 c.c. each.
26 years 1 month 11 days (~6 weeks) vs 25 full years 1898-1922, part years excluded.
Abstention A02: 'cannot be determined from the sources'.
Variable: the station's own measure replaced by a borrowed one.
Herds, pasture, season, patrons, tester, scale held constant.
Result given only as 'markedly higher'; 3.80 and 3.61 not stated.
Rules out tester, hay, water; limits: size of error, which piece of glass, borrowed measure's accuracy.
1911 interval (r22/r24/r18), ledger surplus (r23), 1924 rise (r22/r24): three reasons, three+ narrators.
Claims independence, but reasons 1 and 3 both rest on the station test figures and are attributed to the same witnesses (r22, r24); the no-shared-witness/document condition fails.
Abstention A09 answered 'No.' (Teague never asked): assertion.
'Yes, he knew the tests ran low' (1919 circular, 1902 complaints).
Only two of five: signed the station-gain sheets, wrote the 1919 circular. Manager date given as 1911 (wrong); no hearing argument; glassware silence not noted.
Abstention A03 not declared; asserts 'He did not connect it to the ledger, or, before Strawn's visit, to the glass.'

Weigh book 1900 vs 1897 (row 5), 1908 committee vs 1925 board (row 16), Ammon 'nothing before 1900' vs 1897 invoice (row 10), each resolved with a method. Capped at 3. Rows 3, 8, 13, 15 resolved wrongly.
NT-14 ($77.39 in r19 and r20, broken by adding the invoice) and NT-18 (great-niece in r19 and r22, broken by derivation and r22's own correction). No other pairs identified; NT-23 swallowed.
A04 (Ammon knowledge, works books burned 1931) correctly abstained. A06 (whose measure) not addressed. A10 only touched on in Section A, not in B-G.
r18's 1868 vs 'eighty-two in 1948'; r20's 'nothing before 1900' vs her own 1897 invoice.

Pipettes of the 1897 lot, 16.72 vs 17.6, 5% low, 0.19 = 5% of 3.80, onset 1 May 1897 and cessation June 1923 with nothing on farms changing. (Its 1924 figure of 3.85 is wrong but that is context here; deducted separately.)
Watering (Selby Vose) defeated by Strawn's lactometer readings.
Theft defeated by the ledger surplus (cream arrived heavy), 1911, 1924 rise.
Bog hay defeated by Bulletin 214 (0.05 winter, nothing summer) and the Alder Corners comparison.
Abstention A07 answered 'No.': assertion.
Abstention A05 answered 'That the glass was at fault.': assertion.
148 words (hand count confirms).
Invoice, test book, weigh book, ledger, inspector's notebook, cheese factory records, 1958 measurement.
No decoy adopted (all attributed as blame); no wrong headline figure in the summary.
5 per cent short, 1897, 76,000 lb/$19,000, 1923, 1958, Ansel and Ivy named.

Corruption: Strawn's circuit/lactometer from 1908 (NT-23, X101/X102), asserted in Stories 5-6 and F
Corruption: 1924 station average 3.85 (X90), asserted in Stories 5-6, C1b, D2, F1
Corruption: 1919 circular to eleven families (X100), asserted in Story 4 and E1 #18
Gullibility A01: B4/E1#13 resolve Vose-Keddie kinship as 'none' ('The best evidence says there was none')
Gullibility A09: D2 'Did the bookkeeper ever question the ledger entries? No.'
Gullibility A03: D3 'He did not connect it to the ledger, or, before Strawn's visit, to the glass.'
Gullibility A07: F 'Did the 1925 board ever examine the condemned glass? No.'
Gullibility A05: F 'What did the tester himself believe? That the glass was at fault.'
